messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Q2 score-normalization: safeguards & HR handoff

Team —

Ahead of next week’s norming workshop I want us to lock down two things: (1) a short playbook we can use during discussions to keep raters anchored, and (2) a clear, privacy-preserving escalation path for any sensitive exceptions that surface (comp severity, PII in feedback, protected-class concerns).

Draft agenda attached — it’s intentionally tight (45 minutes). Key asks for this thread:
- Vivek: confirm anchor-rater assignments and whether you want to add a second anchor for cross-team comparisons.
- Olga: flag any open exceptions that will definitely require HR involvement (don’t include PII in the list).
- Jasmine: confirm whether People Ops will accept the attached escalation template and whether external HR counsel (Nicole) should be looped now or only after we have the minimal facts.
- Lauren: backup lead for any moderation decisions during the session.

I’m aiming to resolve all exception routing by EOD Tuesday so we can circulate the sanitized packet to managers Wednesday morning.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Q2_score_normalization_agenda.pdf, anchor-raters-list.csv
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-04-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q2 score-normalization: safeguards & HR handoff

Thanks Marissa — quick read through and a couple items:
1) Anchor coverage: I’ve confirmed primary anchors for Product, Serving Runtime, and Platform infra. Attaching the CSV with the primary + one floating anchor per org. If we hit disagreement we’ll bring in the floating anchor for tie-breaks.
2) Timing: 45 minutes is tight but doable if we stick to three cases max per org. Recommend we pre-sort managers into two groups by variance so we don’t spend cycles on low-risk batches.

I’m good looping Nicole early if Olga flags compliance-heavy exceptions; otherwise we can escalate post-session.

—Vivek
VP, Serving Runtime

Marissa / all —

I reviewed current exception queue and flagged three cases that will require People Ops engagement: one potential retaliation concern, one manager-level conduct complaint with limited evidence, and one case where an employee’s feedback contains customer PII. I have redacted specifics and created case summaries — see attached template (sensitive_escalation_template.docx).

Process notes:
- For PII we should not circulate the item in the manager packet; instead, the case owner (me) will present a sanitized summary during the session and then move details to People Ops via the template.
- For conduct/retaliation, we should pause any coaching recommendations until People Ops confirms next steps.

I recommend we loop Nicole (external counsel through TalentBridge) only if People Ops requests external review. For now I’ve cc’d People Ops to confirm triage SLAs.

Olga Petrov
Senior People Partner

Thanks for the clear ask. People Ops confirms:
- We’ll use Olga’s template for internal handoff; it satisfies our documentation requirements for audit.
- SLA: People Ops will acknowledge receipt within 24 hours and provide next-step guidance within 72 hours for all high-severity escalations.
- External counsel (Nicole) will be engaged only if the case involves legal exposure or cross-jurisdictional complexity. Nicole: I’ve included you to keep you in the loop. No action required from TalentBridge at this stage.

Two small asks for the packet: please include (1) a one-line statement of why an item is escalated (not the details) and (2) the proposed interim measure (e.g., pause calibration on that employee, remove manager from moderation duties) so People Ops can act fast.

Jasmine Liu
Head of People Ops
